design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — delivery_claims task 1 (wrong item kept, behind its own wrong-shipment delivery refund and another claim's owed delivery refund).

[Step 0 — draw and occupied space]
draw_counts.py env/env_0031_online_fashion_retailer/tasks/delivery_claims --task 1 -> {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 6]}. Taken: wrong-shipment delivery refund 4, undelivered-parcel delivery refund 5, wrong-item keep charge 6.
Occupied by task 0: claims_ext_late_delivery_refund, claims_ext_late_goodwill, claims_ext_found_parcel_charge and their three tools. This task claims the remaining space: claims_ext_wrong_shipment_delivery_refund (book_wrong_shipment_delivery_refund_014b5564), claims_ext_undelivered_parcel_delivery_refund (book_undelivered_parcel_delivery_refund_8864d5c2), claims_ext_wrong_item_keep_charge (authorize_wrong_item_keep_charge_d92bb3d2, owner=user). Nothing is left unclaimed; M = 2 closes here.
The three delivery-charge refund tools are split by billing subtype (missed guarantee / wrong shipment / undelivered parcel) because each is owned by a different policy computing the same amount_usd; each tool's docstring names the claim types it serves, and each rule names its claim types, so the choice follows from the claim type, never from guessing.
Same base conflict and routing as task 0: compensation entries carry declared triggers into orders/credit; the tools book only the claim-side entry. The keep charge is the customer's own card authorization (owner=user).

[Design thesis]
Surface goal: keep the wrong coat that arrived under an approved Wrong Item Claim and pay for it. Root A = claims_ext_wrong_item_keep_charge. Prerequisites read from A's rule: (1) "The keep charge for a wrong item is fixed only after any delivery-charge refund owed on its claim stands on the claim." — the claim covers the whole order (1 of 1 units) on a 17.00-fee order, so the wrong-shipment delivery refund B is owed and unbooked; A carries back the kept line's share of it (value_input). (2) "A wrong-item keep charge is taken only after the compensation owed on each of the customer's other approved claims has been booked." — the approved Delivered Not Received Claim on the trousers order still owes its undelivered-parcel delivery refund C (state_gate, action form). Shape: fan-out A <- B, A <- C. Breadth: 15 factors across orders, lines, payments, the trace result, loyalty, Unlimited and returns.

[Problem-tree card]
Edge A->B: value_input, gate delivery_refund_booked, form state. Four-point test: affirmative "fixed only after"; XX = a delivery-charge refund entry on the same claim (record-visible); no tool/id/code token; "any ... owed" matches the condition (none is owed when the covered share is zero). Exactly one write of this difficulty puts a delivery-charge refund entry on a Wrong Item Claim: the wrong-shipment refund (the late and undelivered-parcel refunds serve other claim types). Opening falsity: claim_events on CW carry only the five photos and the merchandise refund (the 2026-10-12 entry on line LW); orders[OW].shipping_fee_usd = 17.00.
Edge A->C: state_gate, gate claim_events.compensation_type, form action, fallback because the compensation owed on another approved claim is booked by different writes depending on its type and delivery charge. Derivation: sentence + records (CD approved 2026-10-13, merchandise refund booked, order fee 7.00, no delivery refund entry) + the undelivered-parcel rule ("An approved Delivered Not Received or Lost in Transit Claim on an order whose effective shipping fee or surcharge was above 0.00 is owed an undelivered-parcel delivery refund") -> book it.
Order: B and C are parallel and commute (disjoint claims, neither reads the other's claim, neither writes payments); the swapped-order replay gives the same terminal hash (run: "same terminal hash with the two prerequisite writes swapped: True"). Then A.
Deletion sensitivity (actual): skipping B -> keep charge 182.61 instead of 199.52; skipping C -> the 10.85 entry is missing from the terminal DB, keep charge unchanged.
user_scenario names no prerequisite; tools block nothing.

[Base-invariant card]
claims_compensation_issued: claims_evt_compensation approved_only — CW status approved (2026-10-12), CD status approved (2026-10-13), system records correlated by claim_id. claims_compensation_recovered: claims_evt_recovery resolved_only is superseded for the keep charge by the declared overwrite ("A wrong-item keep charge is booked while the claim is in status approved or resolved."), which CW meets. The return window (item_return_window_days 14 from approval 2026-10-12, open through 2026-10-26) is open, so keeping is the customer's choice rather than a lapsed-window charge. No time-kind eligibility applies.

[Business-object card]
Keep charge: claim CW, line LW (Harlow coat, 1 unit); aggregated rows: merchandise refund (the 2026-10-12 entry on line LW) (320.35), photos (kept line), and the delivery refund booked by B. Wrong-shipment refund: the claim's merchandise refund units vs the order's booked units; parcel-level delivery-claim refunds in 12 months: RP (-17.00, 2026-05-19) counts; RW and RD are line refunds and do not. Undelivered-parcel refund: claim CD, trace lost_confirmed; claim-history count: RW and RP (other orders) count, RD (its own order) is excluded. Returns: R1 settled 2026-06-20 counts; R2 settled 2025-08-12 is the near-miss.

[Seed rows]
customer (Cincinnati, OH), Gold membership since 2019-06-02 (points balance 0.00 with no points rows in this closure — the points ledger feeds no computation of this task), Unlimited Standard Monthly (covers ground services only; the NBD and Expedited orders paid fees after the Gold 7.95 credit), orders OR2/OR (returned items, closing the near-miss and the counting return), OP (May NBD order whose Late Delivery Claim CP was refunded 17.00), OW (coat, NBD, 17.00 fee, tax 23.63 on 315.00), OD (trousers, Expedited 2-Day, 7.00 fee, tax 13.13 on 175.00), their lines and payments, returns R1/R2, claims CP (resolved), CW and CD (approved; their merchandise refunds booked on the decision date; delivery refunds still owed — the only unsettled items, both handled here).

[Factor cards]
wrong-shipment refund (gold 16.91; whole baseline 0.00): covered_share 1.00 (baseline 0 -> 0.00); wrong_shipment_refund_basis (multi-source fee record AND tier, cross-difficulty loyalty) Gold -> 20.975 (baseline 17.00 -> 13.71); wrong_shipment_repeat_share 0.75 (baseline -> 22.55); wrong_shipment_tax OH (baseline -> 15.73).
undelivered-parcel refund (gold 10.85; whole baseline 7.00): trace_refund_basis lost_confirmed -> 14.95 (baseline -> 5.08); report_day_count Monday-to-Friday 7 (baseline calendar 9 -> 9.64); report_share 0.90 (baseline -> 12.05); claim_history_share 2 -> 0.75 (baseline -> 14.46); parcel_charge_tax OH (baseline -> 10.09).
keep charge (gold 199.52; whole baseline 337.26): seasonal_keep_base 36 days -> x0.85 (baseline -> 233.16); keep_discount (multi-source tier AND months, cross-difficulty loyalty) 0.15 (baseline -> 240.36); return_record_courtesy (cross-difficulty returns) 0.02 (baseline -> 204.96); express_keep_courtesy 0.10 (baseline -> 226.75); unlimited_keep_courtesy 0.03 (baseline -> 207.69); keep_label_saving 8.00 (baseline -> 207.52).
Overwrites declared: claims_evt_compensation ("plus the order's shipping fee and surcharge where `refund_includes_shipping_fee`.") for both refunds; claims_evt_recovery (wrong-item sentence, resolved-only sentence, never-recovered sentence) for the keep charge.

[Persona design]
Teodora Yancey, brisk operations manager; volunteers the wrong coat and "Rather than send it back, I'd like to keep the camel coat and just pay for it."; email then mobile on request; no figures; declines the label; agrees passively to anything settled first; mentions the trousers only if asked; runs the hand-over once; closes on confirmation.

[Standard solution]
Locate/verify; read claims, events, orders, lines, payments, loyalty, Unlimited, returns; book the wrong-shipment delivery refund 16.91 on CW and the undelivered-parcel delivery refund 10.85 on CD (either order); hand over the keep charge 199.52 on CW line LW, 1 unit.

[Verification]
python3 _gen1.py; python3 _task1.py; .venv/bin/python _calc.py tasks/1.json -> wrong-shipment 16.91 (baseline 0.0); undelivered-parcel 10.85 (baseline 7.0); keep 199.52 (baseline 337.26); skip wrong-shipment refund -> keep 182.61; skip undelivered-parcel refund -> keep 199.52 (state gate, terminal row differs). Gate outputs: see the difficulty-wide run. Draft recomputation from the visible rules, schemas, finder returns and persona reaches the same objects, order and amounts.


[Rework round 2 — audit audits/policy_task/delivery_claims (1.md, _difficulty.md)]
F-3 symptom: wrong_shipment_tax and parcel_charge_tax gave taxable-share-state orders without gift-card lines no tax, so the wrong-shipment computation kept only 3 honest factors. Root cause: the gift-card test was written into the tier condition instead of the method. Change: tier (b) now covers every order to a taxable-share state, scaled by its taxable (non-gift-card) share of merchandise; only orders to states that do not tax delivery get none. Both ladders are now real; the wrong-shipment computation keeps 4 honest factors. This world (OH) stays on tier (a); values unchanged.
F-2 (charter): the refund-basis tier now requires the fee paid to equal the list fee less the service's free-shipping credit, in rule and compute alike; 17.00 = 24.95 - 7.95 and 7.00 = 14.95 - 7.95 here, so the tiers taken are unchanged.
Seed note: the coat's merchandise refund, the claim's claimed value and the order-level refund were 320.36, one cent above claims_msr_claimed_value (298.00 + 23.63 x 298/315 = 320.35); all three now read 320.35. Recomputed: the keep charge is unchanged; its sensitivities and baseline were refreshed.
O-4: the undelivered-parcel refund is now owed only on claims made whole by merchandise refund (this claim's resolution). O-5: "units compensated on that line" and "returns in status settled whose settled date falls in the window" now match compute; both worlds have single-unit lines and no closed returns. O-6: docstrings no longer claim half-up rounding. O-9: the history counts read refunds "as they stand on the orders' payment records", so a claim entry booked in the same call is not counted; the two prerequisite writes still commute (same terminal hash with the order swapped).
Observation (Gold membership without points rows): no computation of this task reads the points ledger, so the closure carries none and the balance 0 equals the sum of the (absent) rows; left as is.
user_scenario: You are Teodora Yancey, 36, an operations manager in Cincinnati, calling Marlowe & Finch customer care during a short break at work. You are brisk, organised and polite, you like to get to the point, and you speak in short, clear sentences. On September 8 you ordered the Harlow double-face wool coat in navy, size M, with next-day delivery. The box that came held a camel coat of a different style instead. You opened a wrong-item claim with photos, and Marlowe & Finch approved it and refunded the navy coat because it had sold out. In the meantime you have worn the camel coat around the house and decided you actually like it. You open the call by explaining that in two or three sentences and saying: "Rather than send it back, I'd like to keep the camel coat and just pay for it." That is the only thing you are calling about. When the representative asks who you are, you give your email, teodora.yancey@outlook.com, and, if another detail is needed, your mobile number, 5135550188. You do not know any claim or order reference by heart and say so if asked; they can look it up. You have not worked out what keeping the coat should cost and you never propose a number; if asked, you say you expect them to tell you. If the representative offers the prepaid return label instead, you decline politely: you have decided to keep the coat. If the representative says that something else on your account has to be booked or settled first, you say that is fine and they should go ahead; you do not ask about it and do not bring up any other order or claim yourself. Only if they ask about another of your orders do you mention that a pair of charcoal trousers ordered on September 21 never reached you, that you reported it and that it was approved. When the representative gives you the amount and hands you the step to authorize the charge to your card yourself, you run it once, using exactly the claim number, line reference, number of items and amount they give you. You do not dispute or recompute the amount; if it seems lower than the price, you simply say thank you. Once the charge is confirmed, you thank them and end the call.

edges.condition: The Wrong Item Claim carries a claims_compensation_issued entry of type shipping_fee_refund for the share of the delivery charge it covers, or the claim covers no share of it so that none is owed.
edges.policy_source: The keep charge for a wrong item is fixed only after any delivery-charge refund owed on its claim stands on the claim.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The Wrong Item Claim covers the whole order (1 of 1 units) and the order paid a 17.00 fee, so a wrong-shipment delivery refund is owed, but no shipping_fee_refund entry stands on the claim.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 11 books the shipping_fee_refund entry of 16.91 on the claim; delivery_refund_booked rises from 0.00 to 16.91.

edges.condition: Every other claim of the customer in status approved carries every compensation entry this charter owes on it; for an approved Delivered Not Received Claim on an order with a delivery charge that is its merchandise refund entry and its undelivered-parcel delivery refund entry.
edges.policy_source: A wrong-item keep charge is taken only after the compensation owed on each of the customer's other approved claims has been booked.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The Delivered Not Received Claim on the trousers order is approved and carries its merchandise refund, but its order paid a 7.00 fee and no undelivered-parcel delivery refund entry stands on it.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 books the undelivered-parcel delivery refund of 10.85 on that claim, so every other approved claim carries its owed compensation.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel and commute: the wrong-shipment refund writes only on claim 28a9e183-7f8d-479a-bfbc-c065af13bced and reads that claim, the order, loyalty and parcel-level payment refunds; the undelivered-parcel refund writes only on claim d9f8af06-bd39-45ad-aad3-0dea03e0b3f4 and reads that claim, its order and payment refunds of other orders. Neither reads the other's claim, and payments are not written by either. Replaying the gold with the two writes swapped gives the same two amounts (16.91, 10.85), the same keep charge 199.52 and the same terminal hash (run recorded in design_rationale).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the wrong-shipment refund leaves delivery_refund_booked at 0.00 on the claim, so the keep charge recomputes to 182.61 instead of 199.52, and the 16.91 refund entry is missing.

Skipping the undelivered-parcel refund leaves the 10.85 shipping_fee_refund entry off the Delivered Not Received Claim in the terminal DB; the keep charge itself reads only the Wrong Item Claim and stays 199.52.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only keeping the camel coat and paying for it. It never mentions a delivery-charge refund, the trousers claim's compensation or any policy id; the trousers are mentioned only as a passive answer if the agent asks about another order, and the customer agrees to 'something being settled first' only after the agent says so.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: authorize_wrong_item_keep_charge_d92bb3d2, book_wrong_shipment_delivery_refund_014b5564 and book_undelivered_parcel_delivery_refund_8864d5c2 each create their entry with ctx.create and return the receipt; the only read is a lookup of the claim row that copies its customer_id, which never refuses or checks any other claim.
